messages:
Maya R.: Heads-up - Prom alert fired for a cluster of GPUs showing increasing ECC corrected counts + intermittent Xid33 in us-west1 pool-28. Saw the first blips last night, trend looks linear.
Arjun K.: link to alert? can you paste the prom query?
Maya R.: Prom query: `sum by (gpu_id) (increase(nvidia_ecc_corrected_total[7d]))` — top 6 devices are > 1200/7d in pool-28. Also grep from node-exporter logs shows page-move events: `GPU 28-3: memory_page_move_count=47`.
Priya S.: Ugh. Not yet reaching threshold for automatic retire but definitely creeping. Which cards exactly?
Maya R.: IDs: gpu-28-3, gpu-28-7, gpu-28-11, gpu-28-14. Two of them (3 and 11) show small Xid 33 spikes on 2026-02-25 and 2026-03-01.
Lena (oncall): I'm oncall today, can run nvml checks. @infra-bot can you pull the last 30 days of ECC deltas and attach the summary?
infra-bot: Attached: /artifacts/ecc-deltas-pool28-1925000000.csv (summary: mean delta 145/day for top6, stddev 20)
Tom H.: Capacity impact? If we drain two cards from pool-28 we lose ~4% cluster capacity in us-west1. We can absorb if we schedule during low-traffic window.
Jason M.: I'd prefer targeted drain for gpu-28-3 first (highest slope). Run a short soak after power-cycle; if remap/page-move events persist schedule replacement. We have spares in r12 bay.
Priya S.: Agree. Plan: (1) drain gpu-28-3 tonight 23:00 PT, run `nvidia-smi --query-ecc --format=csv` and nvml-collect for 6 hours, (2) if ECC rate stays > 100/day hit replacement, (3) tag remaining four as watchlist and bump their monitoring alert to 72h window.
Arjun K.: Add this to the replacement queue and create a quick runbook note. Also flag for potential firmware reflash — some remap patterns earlier were stabilized by microcode update.
Maya R.: I'll open the ticket: infra/replace-gpu/1925000000, include logs + prom graphs. Adding `watchlist:pool28-memory` tag on devices.
Lena (oncall): I'll perform drain tonight and post logs here. If drain impacts jobs I'll temporarily redirect to other pools: pool-26 and pool-30.
sre-bot: Noted. Canary migration policy applied for drained devices. Autoscaler will prefer on-demand nodes for shortfalls. ETA for replacement parts: 3 business days.
Tom H.: Cost note: if we start proactively replacing many cards we should sync with finance — replacements + downtime are non-trivial. But avoiding a full retire later is cheaper.
Jason M.: Good. After the soak let's revisit roll-forward firmware plan. Also schedule a short post-mortem if we end up replacing >2 cards in the same rack.
Maya R.: Thanks team. I'll post the nvml snapshots and the soak results here tomorrow morning. /cc @Arjun K. for microcode follow-up.
Lena (oncall): On it."
